body.p: Favorable consideration of this application is respectfully requested in view of the above amendments and the following remarks.

By this Amendment, claims 1 and 7 have been amended. No claims have been added or cancelled. Claims 1-11 and 13-21 are thus currently pending in this application, with claim 1 being the only independent claim. Support for the amendments can be found, for example, in Figs. 6E and 6F and in paragraph [0097] of the published description. No new matter is added.

Claims 1-11 and 13-21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention, mainly for a lack of antecedence of claim term(s).

Claim 1 has been amended as provided herewith to clarify that "the breath from the patient" is --the breath sample from the patient--, as suggested by the examiner, and thereby rendering the rejection moot.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-4, 10, 11, and 14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0093226 to Dr Moschos in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0077093 to Pan and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0110444 to Sherwood et al.

Further, claim 5 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2010/0292601 to Dompeling et al.; claims 6 and 7 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Dompeling, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0035326 to King-Smith; claims 8 and 9 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, Dompeling, King-Smith, U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0119280 to Ahmad et al., and International Patent Application Publication No. WO 2018/071441 to Akouka et al.; claim 13 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view

of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2016/0338616 to Eichler; claim 15 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0173731 to Meka et al.; claim 16 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2012/0004571 to Ku et al.; claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2015/0072889 to Lui et al.; claim 18 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent No. 5,465,728 to Phillips; and claims 19- 21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dr Moschos in view of Pan, Sherwood, and U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0138577 to Kline.
The rejections are respectfully traversed for at least the following reasons.

Independent claim 1 has been amended as provided herewith to recite, in combination with other features, a non-rebreather part that comprises an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler and arranged to be closed by a one-way inlet valve arranged to allow air to enter the non-rebreather part, the air inlet in fluid communication with the first portion of the internal breath flow pathway. This combination of features is neither known nor derivable from the cited references.

Dr Moschos concerns an exhaled breath condensate collection device. The device includes a mouthpiece inner component (120) that comprises a first inner component (121) and a second inner component (123). The mouthpiece inner component is fully seated within a mouthpiece housing component (160) and the mouthpiece breath inlet port (122) and the mouthpiece exhaust outlet port are said to be aligned with the mouthpiece (162) and the mouthpiece exhaust (164). Dr Moschos admittedly does not disclose or suggest a non-rebreather part comprising a one-way outlet valve and an air inlet. The Official Action, therefore, cites Pan to supposedly remedy this deficiency (See Official Action, page 10).

Pan generally relates to a method and apparatus to detect the presence of bacteria in a subject. Pan provides a check valve (115) near the intake end (113) of the tube (107) that restricts flow through the tube at the intake end to a direction toward the mouthpiece end (111) and blocks flow out of the intake end (see Pan at para. [0063] and Fig. 2). However, Pan fails to disclose or suggest slits or openings of any kind in the any of the check valve, intake end, or the tube.

Sherwood was also cited by the Official Action to reject independent claim 1, but solely to teach an air diverter in the sample delivery part arranged to divide the sample delivery part into an upstream portion and a downstream portion. Sherwood lacks any teaching or reasonable suggestion of the recited air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler, and as such, cannot be applied to cure the aforementioned deficiencies of Dr Moschos and Pan.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that Dr Moschos, Pan, and Sherwood, whether taken individually or in combination, fail to disclose, reasonably suggest, or render obvious a breath sampler having all the features of the amended claim 1.

For the sake of completeness, it is recognized that Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline were also cited by the Official Action but solely with respect to features set forth in dependent claims. Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline each lack any disclosure or reasonable suggestion of the recited air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler. Consequently, none of Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline can be applied to remedy the aforementioned deficiencies of Dr Moschos, Pan, and Sherwood.

For at least the reasons discussed herein, it is respectfully submitted that the disclosures in Dr Moschos, Pan, Sherwood, Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline, whether taken individually or in combination, would not have rendered the breath sampler set forth in the amended claim 1 obvious.

The dependent claims are patentable over the cited references at least by virtue of their dependence from independent claim 1. A detailed discussion of the additional distinguishing features recited in the dependent claims is thus not set forth at this time. Applicant reserves the right to present such arguments later during prosecution or appeal.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.

Early and favorable action with respect to this application is respectfully requested. In view of the above amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all of the claims now pending in the instant application should be allowable, and reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.

Should any questions arise in connection with this application or should the Examiner believe that a telephone conference with the undersigned would be helpful in resolving any remaining issues pertaining to this application, the undersigned respectfully requests to be
contacted at the number or email indicated below.
Respectfully submitted,
